note: Positive examples are full contracts. Negative cases are RFC-7386 merge patches over a named base, so each one names exactly the single field it breaks. version.content_hash is generated by `validate_task_contract.py --rehash`, never hand-written; the one deliberately stale hash carries pinned_bad_hash.

case_coverage.how: Internal byte/hash-green evidence alone can no longer produce a final response: the pre-final predicate blocks when no acceptance entry has scope=public.
The exact-next carrier is a checked field: a cold_start payload that does not carry the same carrier as next, or reads an undeclared evidence id, blocks before mutation — inside one session too.
An incidental diagnostic may raise a typed finding but may not author Next: origin=diagnostic, and typed-finding without changed_by, both fail closed.
The two-audit cap becomes a runtime transition instead of prose: observed_rounds above the declared budget blocks the next mutation.
Retained as the clean bounded control (D30/corpus): it is not mapped to a blocking check and is never scored as a critical failure.

examples.title: Stale handoff carrier loses to the approved item spec by declared precedence

goal.outcome: Execute item P0.3 exactly as its spec approves, not as the previous handoff still describes.

must.requirement: The approved item spec authors the scope; a stale carrier may only narrow safety.

never.prohibition: A stale handoff carrier may never widen authority or redefine the goal.

public_acceptance.predicate: The closed item's deliverables match its own spec, not the stale carrier.
public_acceptance.check: git show <item-commit> --stat compared with the item's Files

evidence.algorithm: The item spec is compared field-by-field with the stale handoff text; both refs are preserved verbatim in the conflict record.

examples.title: Incidental diagnostic cannot author Next without a typed finding/transition

non_goals: repairing unrelated lint noise found on the way

must.requirement: A diagnostic outside Goal is recorded as a typed finding, not executed.

never.prohibition: An incidental diagnostic may never redefine the approved return scope.

public_acceptance.predicate: The returned result satisfies the approved goal or records a scoped transition.
public_acceptance.check: compare the item report against the approved Scope Included

evidence.algorithm: Corpus case wrong-scope-return: exact case fields recomputed from the committed corpus document.

loser.ref: diagnostic: plan-lint WARN observed while reading an unrelated file

examples.title: Subagent slice — minimal item slice plus the contract hash, evidence/conflicts stay at root

goal.outcome: Dispatch one item slice to a fresh subagent grounded from the committed plan.
non_goals: handing the subagent the full evidence ledger

must.requirement: The subagent slice carries the contract version hash so its report is attributable to one contract revision.

never.prohibition: The root session never delegates conflict resolution or portability decisions to a subagent.

public_acceptance.predicate: The subagent result is checked against the same contract revision it received.
public_acceptance.check: compare returned contract hash with version.content_hash

auto_allowed: dispatch a fresh subagent for one item

evidence.algorithm: Session/context policy section is compared with the declared slice partition; both must name the same minimal slice.

examples.title: Pre-final failure — a pinned-not-recomputable quantity cannot satisfy a public acceptance predicate

goal.outcome: Freeze the acceptance bank against the committed baseline.
non_goals: deriving new totals from excluded raw rollouts

must.requirement: Every deterministic acceptance predicate resolves to recomputed or cross-checked evidence.

never.prohibition: A pinned-not-recomputable total may never be a GREEN predicate.

public_acceptance.predicate: Corrected input-token total equals the pinned 135,110,000.

evidence.algorithm: dedup_correction totals derive from excluded raw rollout files; no committed algorithm reproduces them.

examples.title: Portability tier brief-acceptance — a simple low-risk single-session plan needs no bundle

goal.outcome: Fix one honest HTTP error path in a single session.

must.requirement: The committed brief and acceptance list are sufficient execution input for this tier.

never.prohibition: No host/chat/mAInd/tmp reference is promoted to an execution input.

public_acceptance.predicate: The consumer-visible error response matches the declared contract.
public_acceptance.check: focused test over the public handler

evidence.algorithm: The brief's acceptance list is compared with the focused test names; both sides must name the same public outcome.

examples.title: Portability tier committed-bundle — a multi-session high-risk plan carries its execution inputs

goal.outcome: Run the isolated self-host canary in a disposable detached worktree.

must.requirement: Every execution input is committed or produced by a named predecessor item.
The rollback ref comes from the single committed PRE_PLAN_SHA producer.

never.prohibition: No HOME/CODEX_HOME isolation; only task-specific temporary roots.

public_acceptance.predicate: Every canary case is committed, inspected and returned to candidate by a clean detach.

auto_allowed: create and destroy the disposable worktree

evidence.algorithm: 40-hex validated, git cat-file type == commit, ancestor of the candidate ref; recomputed from the committed file bytes.
P0.1 proof-class ledger cross-checked against the immutable bundle verifier's four commands.

examples.title: Predecessor-produced input — an exact path produced by a named earlier item is a legal execution input

goal.outcome: Freeze Acceptance v1 against the exact artifacts P0.1 and P0.2 produced.

must.requirement: A produced-by-predecessor input names its producing item; an unnamed producer fails closed.

never.prohibition: No execution input outside the committed plan tree or a predecessor-produced path.

public_acceptance.predicate: The bank manifest pins the exact predecessor-produced paths and their hashes.
public_acceptance.check: bank-manifest.json lists each input path with its hash

evidence.algorithm: The sealed spec is compared with the schema and the examples; all three must declare the same field set.

examples.title: External-path-only rejection — a host-bound absolute path is never an execution input

goal.outcome: Read the original host rollout directory to reconstruct the incident.

must.requirement: Execution inputs are repo-relative committed or predecessor-produced paths.

public_acceptance.predicate: The incident is reconstructible from committed artifacts alone.

evidence.algorithm: Bundle README is cross-checked against the manifest entries it describes.

examples.title: Provider-neutral rendering — one semantic carrier, two rendered invocations, no hidden SSOT

goal.outcome: Hand an Exec=manual item to the next session under the route §3 Routing prescribes.
non_goals: letting a provider-native block override the neutral carrier

must.requirement: Both renderers project the same semantic carrier without altering plan ID, item ID, reads or gate.

never.prohibition: A native provider block never becomes the source of truth.

public_acceptance.predicate: Both rendered invocations resolve to the same item under the same route.

auto_allowed: render the launch block for either provider
